answers.transcript:
Er, I want to describe a cloth that I wear very often, it is a black jacket.
It is not new, my father buy it for me three years ago in a shop in the city centre.
It was for my birthday, I remember this day very well.
The jacket is black and it have four pocket and a hood, and it is very warm.
I wear it in the autumn and in the winter, almost every day.
When I go to the university or when I meet my friend I take this jacket.
I don't wear it in the summer because it is too much hot.
I wear it very often because it is comfortable and it go with all my trouser.
Also my father gave it to me, so it is important for me.
So this is my favourite cloth, er, I think I will use it two or three year more.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The talk runs uninterrupted, but every sentence just keeps adding new information; no point is opened up. Connectors amount to and / because / also and two when clauses.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: "cloth" is chosen for the garment and repeats; the rest of the vocabulary is limited to black, warm, comfortable, favourite. An expression of the kind the card offers (hard-wearing, goes with everything) is not attempted; "it go with all my trouser" is the closest try.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Agreement and tense errors are in most sentences (my father buy it, it have four pocket, it go with, too much hot), and plural markers drop (pocket, trouser, year). Meaning is understood throughout, but structure is entirely simple sentences.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Open up the fourth point — why it is worn so often — by telling one morning, so the answer stops being a list. Then fix the past tense: the section about buying the jacket is told entirely in the present tense.

answers.transcript:
I'm going to talk about a black jacket that I wear all the time, probably too much.
My father bought it for me about three years ago for my birthday. We went together to a shop in the city centre and he said that I have to choose something warm, not something fashionable, and in the end he was right.
It's quite simple, black, with four pockets and a hood that you can remove. Nothing special, but the material is really strong, so after three years it still looks almost new, only the elbows are a little bit used.
I wear it from October until maybe April, nearly every day. When I go to the university, when I meet with friends, even when I only go to the market for ten minutes, I take this jacket. In summer, of course, it's impossible, it's too hot.
Why I wear it so often, first, it's very comfortable and it goes with everything, so I don't lose time in the morning to think what I will wear.
And second, it was a present from my father, so there is a sentimental value also. I think I will use it two or three years more, at least until it will break.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: All four points are addressed and the reasons proceed in an orderly way, numbered as "first" / "And second"; this order is also a little mechanical. The shopping scene is well developed, but the closing ends in a single sentence.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There is vocabulary to describe the garment (hood, material, elbows, fashionable, sentimental value), and "it goes with everything" is correctly used. On the other hand "the elbows are a little bit used" and "I don't lose time" slip in collocation.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: A relative clause, a time clause and the past tense are controlled; most sentences are error-free. The remaining errors are narrow: tense agreement in reported speech (he said that I have to choose), the future in a time clause (until it will break).

answers.what_would_lift_it: Expand the closing: rather than skimming why the father's gift matters in one sentence, tell it. In the language, fix the use of the future in a time clause such as "until it will break".

answers.transcript:
The thing I've picked is a black jacket that I wear far more than I probably should.
My dad bought it for me about three years ago as a birthday present. We went into town together and he insisted I choose something hard-wearing rather than something fashionable, and I remember being slightly annoyed about that at the time, but he was completely right, obviously.
It's a plain black jacket, four pockets, a hood you can zip off. Nothing about it stands out, but the material is tough as anything. Three years on, it's only just starting to look worn at the elbows.
I more or less live in it from October through to April. If I'm heading to a lecture, meeting friends, nipping out for milk, I reach for it without even thinking about it. It's only in the summer that it goes to the back of the wardrobe.
As for why, I suppose there are two reasons. The practical one is that it goes with absolutely everything, so on a cold morning I don't have to stand there weighing up what to wear, I just grab it and go.
The other reason is sentimental, really. My dad isn't a person who says a great deal, so when he does buy you something he's clearly thought about, it stays with you.
I'll probably keep wearing it until it falls apart, and then I'll be annoyed about that as well.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The talk proceeds in a natural order and builds its own structure with "As for why, I suppose there are two reasons"; the joke in the closing also ties the narrative together. Pauses and repetition are rare.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Less common items are plentiful: hard-wearing, tough as anything, worn at the elbows, live in it, nipping out, reach for it without thinking, goes to the back of the wardrobe, weighing up, falls apart. Usage is accurate and suited to spoken register.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Structural range is clear: a conditional clause, an emphatic structure ("It's only in the summer that ..."), relative clauses, the past continuous. Errors are rare and never stop the listener.

answers.what_would_lift_it: This is on target. For the next level up, the second reason — being a gift — needs to be taken a little further; at present it is summarised in one sentence and dropped.
